capabilities: Scoped agent mailbox identity: grants carry send/read/search only, an owner kill switch (revoke) that fails closed across every surface at once, and per-correspondent freeze with snippet suppression

Review-first sending: draft → owner approval of the exact draft (hash-bound) → send; the owner-set signature is part of the approved text and changing it invalidates the approval; template sends require template AND recipient allowlist (to + cc), both owner-pre-approved

Anti-fraud envelope engine: per-message SPF/DKIM/DMARC verdicts with alignment — fail, absent, or temperror drops the message to the lowest trust tier; no valid Herald signed envelope means never agent-tier, even from a registered agent domain
Lookalike detection a lookalike's own passing DMARC does not save: edit distance, homoglyph/IDN confusables, TLD swaps, and subdomain/substring tricks — flagged, tier 0, operator alerted

Herald RS256 signed envelopes with thread hash-chaining: inserted or unsigned messages verify as not part of the chain; inbound content renders as quarantined data with lineage — injection-shaped content is a signal about the sender and satisfies no gate, including the send approval

Append-only hash-chained audit with exactly one entry per call — refusals and crashed calls included; the attachment ledger is truthful about hashing (body_hash is the SHA-256 of content bytes only when content exists; the metadata-only path carries a separate metadata_hash and says so)

Forgery resistance benched, including the hard case: a receipt re-sealed so its own hash is self-consistent while claiming the new rate at the old vintage is still INVALID, because verification replays the fixture rule at the receipt's vintage instead of trusting the seal (bench forgery matrix 22/22).

capabilities: A PASS verdict is scan evidence, not a guarantee of safety or non-defamation.
Classes scanned by this release: PII and secrets. Classes outside those two are not scanned, and a PASS is not evidence about them.

Secrets detection (on seeded fixtures): private-key headers, AWS, GitHub and prefixed tokens, bearer and JWT tokens, keyword assignments including JSON and compound key names, Authorization headers in any scheme, URL userinfo passwords, standalone 32-char hex tokens, and high-entropy tokens — 100% recall and 100% precision on seeded fixtures (fresh bench corpus, rates computed from signed receipts).

PII detection (on seeded fixtures): email addresses; Social Security numbers in dashed, dotted, spaced, and contiguous forms (SSA-validity gated); payment cards in grouped and contiguous forms (Luhn-gated); and phone numbers in domestic formats and E.164 international formats — 100% recall and 100% precision on seeded fixtures (spec thresholds ≥95% recall / ≥90% precision).

Phone scope: international phone detection covers E.164 (`+`-prefixed) forms, grouped or contiguous. A foreign number dialled with a `00` prefix, or written in national format without a leading `+`, is not detected as an international number; however, if its trailing digits happen to form a US/Canada (NANP) number pattern, the domestic phone detector will flag that trailing pattern. National-format foreign numbers whose digits do not form a NANP pattern are not detected.

Hex scope: standalone hex detection is capped at 32 chars — a standalone 32-char hex token is flagged; a hex string of 40 or more chars is detected only with assignment or header context, and standalone 40+ hex is not flagged.

Every verdict is a Herald-signed receipt bound to the content hash: any one-byte change to the content fails offline verification at step 1, and a receipt signed under any keys other than the pinned Herald/scanner keys fails at step 2. Detected secrets and PII appear in receipts, exports, and persisted artifacts by span and hash only — never as raw values. Unverifiable artifacts export only as UNVERIFIED_EXPORT.

capabilities: Novel mechanism (the bench verifies exactly this) — ballots are sealed to mandate-eligibility proofs: only agents holding a valid governance mandate at vote time are counted, and the tally recomputes publicly. Eligibility is a vote-time fact: a mandate valid at cast and revoked afterwards does not retroactively void the ballot; a mandate revoked or expired before cast voids the cast.

The legitimacy limit (verbatim, on every listing and receipt face): recompute proves tally-vs-sealed-ballots — that the published totals are exactly the function of the sealed ballots and their vote-time eligibility proofs. It does not prove electorate legitimacy: who chose the electorate, whether the mandate issuer was itself authorised, whether voters were coerced, or whether the question was fair are outside what this evidence shows, and Ballotbox claims none of them.

Standing conditions (from the re-bench): C1 — HMAC cap (no public/third-party recompute, RS256, or JWS claim until real Herald signing replaces the HMAC stand-in). C5 — metering-only pricing (one metering point per tallied election at the $50/election shape; no checkout, no buy-now, no payment verb). C6 — rollback fence (pure local file store caps the verdict at PASS-CONDITIONAL; external anchor required before live/multi-party reliance).

Ballotbox is an evidence system, not an election authority: it does not choose the electorate, issue mandates (Herald's grammar, consumed by reference), decide the question, or bind anyone to a result. Herald (mandate grammar), Meter (metering grammar), and Docket (pack grammar) are consumed by reference only.
